checks: Turbo is supported by the exact detected TCL112AC protocol; a manufacturer name or TCL96AC does not invent support.
Six page engines follow received TCL112AC rather than an incorrect saved brand, without rewriting the database profile.
Legacy kMax fan is High; a checksummed packet with Turbo OFF stays OFF across all six pages.
Old Generic capability cache cannot hide a feature supported by the received protocol.
Legacy Turbo ON is taken from the independent Turbo bit, together with the received swing flag.
Production dashboard separates High fan from active Turbo.
Production Schedule mode summary includes the actual received Turbo flag separately from High fan.
Explicit receiver flags update Turbo, Swing and Eco, while the receiver manifest excludes unsupported functions.
Auxiliary packets and noise preserve the last full observation and supported controls.
Truncated or corrupt legacy packets leave Turbo unknown instead of inferring it from fan speed.
Explicit firmware-decoded fields take priority over the compatibility reader.
Receiver protocol identifiers normalize case and accept raw_type when protocol is absent.
Manual protocol overrides that contradict the receiver are rejected without a cloud command.
Turbo ON and OFF dispatch separate flags using the detected protocol, with normal High fan and honest Queued delivery.
A receiver manifest denying Turbo hides and rejects it without queuing a command.
Malformed capability strings, fan names and temperature ranges cannot enable controls.
A new valid received protocol replaces the previous capability family across all six engines.
